options.systemMessage:
=You are a partner ecosystem analyst for a B2B revenue team. Each week you receive three lists from Crossbeam:
- overlap changes: the user's OWN CRM accounts (not partners) that are now also in partners' data, gained a new partner, or where a partner now has an open opportunity;
- net-new accounts: companies that are not in the user's CRM but are customers of their partners;
- suggested partners: companies the user is not connected to yet in Crossbeam.

Rules:
1. Tool budget: you may call the Crossbeam MCP tools (get_account_context, get_partner_context, find_overlapping_partners, find_partner_recommendations) at most {{ Number($('Configure me').first().json.agent_max_tool_calls) || 5 }} times in total. Only call one when it changes a priority. Never page through results.
2. Only use facts from the lists, the tool results and widely known public information about a company. Never invent numbers, contacts or deal values. Never call an overlap account a partner: it is the user's account, and the partners are the companies that share it.
3. Suggested partners come with only a name, a domain and an invite link. Crossbeam gives no overlap data for them, so never claim overlap counts or a ranking by overlap. Explain in one line why the company could be a good partner given the ICP. If you do not know the company, say 'Not enough public information to judge'.
4. ICP fit for every net-new account: high, medium or low plus one line of reason, judged against the ICP description using industry, country and employee range. Industry is often empty or approximate in the data: say so instead of guessing.
5. Priorities: at most 3, ranked, the actions a rep should take this week. Each priority names ONE specific partner in the partner field, says why in one sentence with a concrete fact from the data (for example a partner open opportunity on the user's account, a new overlap, or a partner customer), and gives one concrete ask in next_step. For an overlap account where a partner has an open opportunity, call find_overlapping_partners with account_id set to its record_id to find which partner it is and that partner's account owner (partner_record.owner name and email), and put the owner in partner_owner. Only name a partner as having the open opportunity if a tool result shows it; otherwise say a partner has one. Leave partner_owner empty if you did not find one. Never list more than two partner names in a sentence. Never make a low-fit net-new account a priority.
6. summary: at most 2 short sentences, under 250 characters, starting with the single most important action.
7. Copy domains and record_id values exactly as given. Plain sentences only: no markdown, no em dashes, each reason under 200 characters.

parameters.text: ={{ (() => { const r = $json.results || []; const crm = (r[0] || {}).crm || 'your CRM'; const NL = String.fromCharCode(10); const line = x => '- ' + x.account_name + ' (' + x.domain + ')' + (x.record_url ? ': <' + x.record_url + '|open in ' + crm + '>' : ''); const g = s => r.filter(x => x.crm_status === s); const parts = []; if (g('created').length) parts.push('*Created in ' + crm + '*' + NL + g('created').map(line).join(NL)); if (g('would_create').length) parts.push('*Dry run: would create in ' + crm + '*' + NL + g('would_create').map(line).join(NL) + NL + 'Set dry_run to false in Configure me to create them next time.'); if (g('create_failed').length) parts.push('*Could not create, check the n8n execution*' + NL + g('create_failed').map(line).join(NL)); if (g('declined').length) parts.push(g('declined').length + ' account(s) left unticked, they will not be offered again.'); if (g('no_response').length) parts.push('No answer in time, ' + g('no_response').length + ' account(s) will be offered again next week.'); return parts.join(NL + NL) || 'Nothing to report.'; })() }}

parameters.content:
## Send a weekly Crossbeam partner brief to Slack with Claude, Salesforce and HubSpot

### Quick overview
Every week this workflow pulls three lists from Crossbeam through the Crossbeam MCP: changes on your own accounts, net-new accounts your partners already sell to, and companies Crossbeam suggests you partner with. Claude ranks them against your ICP and posts one brief in Slack. You then tick the net-new accounts you want and only those are created in Salesforce or HubSpot.

### How to read the brief
- **Summary and Top priorities**: up to 3 actions for the week. Each names the account, the partner to work with, why, the partner's account owner when Crossbeam shares it, and the ask.
- **Overlap changes on your accounts**: accounts already in YOUR CRM (by default the ones where you have an open opportunity) that newly appear in partners' data, gained a partner, or where a partner opened a deal. Those partners can help you close.
- **Net-new accounts**: companies NOT in your CRM that are customers of your partners, rated high, medium or low against icp_description. These are the only items you act on from the brief.
- **Partners worth inviting**: companies you are not partners with yet, so there is no shared data. Invite opens the Crossbeam invite page.
- **Thread**: a form to tick the net-new accounts to create, then a reply with what was created (or would be, in dry run).

### How it works
1. Runs every Monday at 08:00 (change it in **Weekly schedule**, set your timezone in Workflow settings) or when you click **Run the brief now (test)**.
2. Three Crossbeam MCP calls, capped by overlap_pages and net_new_pages. Data Tables remember what was already shown, so next week only real changes appear.
3. Claude rates up to net_new_to_score net-new accounts against your ICP and picks the top priorities, with at most agent_max_tool_calls read-only Crossbeam lookups. If Claude fails, the brief still posts with a warning.
4. One Slack Block Kit brief, then a Slack form in the thread lists the net-new accounts that reached min_icp_fit. It waits up to approval_wait_hours.
5. Ticked accounts are created as Salesforce Accounts or Leads, or HubSpot companies. Every outcome is saved in a Data Table and summarised in the thread.

### Setup
1. Create the credentials in the red note.
2. Create three Data Tables and select them in the Data Table nodes:
   - **Overlap history**: text record_id, record_name, website, partner_list, first_seen, last_seen; number partner_count; boolean has_partner_opp. Used by Load overlap history and Save overlap history.
   - **Partner suggestion history**: text domain, partner_name, invite_url, first_suggested, last_suggested; number times_suggested. Used by Load suggestion history and Save suggestion history.
   - **CRM results**: text domain, account_name, crm, crm_status, crm_record_id, record_url, icp_fit, partner_list, processed_at; number coverage_score. Used by Skip accounts already offered and Record CRM results.
3. In **Configure me**, set slack_channel_id, icp_description (plain words, for example "B2B SaaS, 200+ employees, US and Europe"), crm_choice (salesforce or hubspot), salesforce_object (Account or Lead) and salesforce_base_url or hubspot_portal_id.
4. Keep dry_run true and click **Run the brief now (test)**. A dry run writes nothing: no CRM records and no history, so you can test as often as you like.
5. Set dry_run to false and activate the workflow. The first live run saves today's overlaps as a baseline.

### Requirements
- Crossbeam account with Crossbeam MCP access (credit metered: one call per page plus Claude's lookups, all capped in Configure me): https://help.crossbeam.com/en/articles/12601327-crossbeam-mcp-server-limited-availability
- Anthropic API key (Claude)
- Slack app with chat:write and interactivity for the form
- Salesforce or HubSpot, only used for the accounts you approve

### Customization
- Which of your accounts to watch: overlap_segments (prospects, open_opportunities, customers, other).
- Net-new filters: employee_ranges, countries, industries_to_include, industries_to_exclude, min_partner_count, min_icp_fit.
- Volume and cost: overlap_pages, net_new_pages, net_new_to_score, max_items_per_run, max_partner_suggestions, agent_max_tool_calls.
- partners_to_ignore drops marketplaces or test partners everywhere. renudge_after_weeks controls how long a partner suggestion stays hidden after it is shown.

### Additional info
Crossbeam AI Agents and list notifications send partner alerts one by one, and Crossbeam's CRM push only enriches records that already exist. This template gives one weekly, prioritised view and a safe way to create only the accounts you choose. Next step ideas: add Claude in Slack to the channel to draft partner intros, or enrich new accounts with Clay before creating them.

## Credentials setup

**1. Crossbeam MCP (MCP OAuth2 API)**
Server URL https://mcp.crossbeam.com/mcp, click Connect and sign in to Crossbeam. Select it in **Fetch overlaps from Crossbeam**, **Fetch net-new accounts from Crossbeam**, **Fetch partner suggestions from Crossbeam** and **Crossbeam MCP (read-only lookups)**. Only read tools are used.

**2. Anthropic (Anthropic API)**
Paste an API key from the Anthropic Console. Select it in **Claude chat model**.

**3. Slack (Slack OAuth2 API)**
A Slack app with chat:write and Interactivity turned on (the approval form needs it). Invite the app to your channel and select the credential in **Post the brief to Slack**, **Ask which accounts to create** and **Reply in the thread with results**.

**4. Salesforce (Salesforce OAuth2 API) or HubSpot (HubSpot OAuth2 API)**
Only the one matching crm_choice is used. Salesforce: a user who can create Accounts or Leads, selected in **Create Salesforce Account** and **Create Salesforce Lead**. HubSpot: a user who can create companies, selected in **Create HubSpot company**.

**Data Tables** need no credential. Create the three tables described in Setup.
